mode_reason: Core flow gate passed. 6 Tier 1 issues identified from user focus requirements but no reliability blockers. Normal mode allows all tiers to receive pipelines.

issues.description: LaTeX rendering silently broken: MarkdownView.tsx has no case for 'latex' block type, so LatexRenderer.tsx (fully implemented) is never invoked. LaTeX content parsed by parseMarkdown.ts as type 'latex' falls through to null and is silently dropped. Browser-verified: raw '$$E = mc^2$$' text appears instead of typeset math.
issues.details: parseMarkdown.ts:24 defines 'latex' block type. LatexRenderer.tsx is a complete KaTeX-based renderer. MarkdownView.tsx renderContent() handles: text, header, horizontal-rule, list, numbered-list, code-block, mermaid, options, table, image -- but has NO 'latex' case. The block falls through to the else clause returning null. Fix requires adding an import of LatexRenderer and a case branch for block.type === 'latex'.
issues.observation_notes: All 4 agents independently confirmed this issue via code review and/or browser testing. User agent browser-verified raw text rendering. Architect confirmed hasRenderedMath=false in DOM evaluation. PO traced the exact code path. UI-specialist grep confirmed no 'latex' string in MarkdownView.tsx.

issues.description: File attachment/upload button missing from input toolbar. useAttachments.ts hook and AttachmentStrip.tsx component exist in codebase but are never imported or referenced in AgentInput.tsx or SessionView.tsx. Server upload endpoint POST /v3/sessions/:id/upload exists. The UI wiring was lost during merge with origin.
issues.details: useAttachments.ts at sources/hooks/useAttachments.ts is fully implemented (pickImage, pickDocument, addFileFromPaste, clearAttachments). AttachmentStrip.tsx component exists. Neither is imported in AgentInput.tsx. The AgentInput component has no onAttachPress prop. Server-side upload routes exist at v3SessionRoutes.ts:247. The sync layer sendMessage() accepts an attachments parameter. All backend infrastructure is in place -- only the UI entry point in AgentInput is missing.
issues.observation_notes: All 4 agents confirmed: toolbar shows gear, info, git-diff badge, send/mic button only. No paperclip/attachment icon. PO identified specific file locations. Architect confirmed server endpoint exists. User verified on both desktop and mobile viewports.

issues.description: 'wrap' envelope type renders as 'Unknown event' instead of collapsible skill/command prompt. typesRaw.ts correctly normalizes wrap envelopes to {type: 'wrapped', label, content} but AgentEventBlock in MessageView.tsx has no case for type 'wrapped'. Falls through to default 'Unknown event' text.
issues.details: AgentEventBlock handles: type==='switch', type==='message', type==='limit-reached'. No case for type==='wrapped'. The 'wrapped' event has label and content fields from typesRaw.ts:577-587 normalization. It should render as a collapsible block showing the label as header and content as body. This is the 'wrap' envelope type defined in sessionProtocol.ts for skill/command prompts (slash commands).
issues.observation_notes: PO, architect, and UI-specialist all traced the code path independently. Not browser-verified because no test sessions contained wrap envelope data, but code analysis is conclusive: the 'wrapped' type has no handler in the switch.

issues.description: Enter key in message input field does not send message. On web, MultiTextInput.tsx uses submitBehavior='newline' which inserts a newline before the React onKeyPress handler can call preventDefault(). User agent observed Enter key navigating to a different session URL instead of sending. The expected behavior (Enter sends, Shift+Enter newline) is broken.
issues.details: User agent browser-verified: pressing Enter in the input field navigated to session 2 URL instead of sending. UI-specialist traced code: MultiTextInput.tsx:222 sets submitBehavior='newline', and the setting agentInputEnterToSend defaults to true in settings.ts:89. The conflict between submitBehavior='newline' and the Enter-to-send setting means the native textarea behavior fires before React can intercept it. The user agent confirmed this across multiple attempts.
issues.observation_notes: User agent observed actual navigation on Enter press (browser-verified). UI-specialist confirmed via code analysis that submitBehavior='newline' conflicts with Enter-to-send expectation. This breaks the most fundamental keyboard interaction pattern for a chat application.

issues.description: File download support entirely absent from the app. No download button, save icon, or download link exists anywhere. Users can view file content in tool call detail views but cannot save it. Server has GET /files/* route for serving files, but no UI affordance triggers downloads.
issues.details: User explicitly flagged file download as a major gap vs Claude Desktop/ChatGPT/Gemini. PO confirmed no download button in tool detail views or message content. Architect confirmed fileRoutes.ts has GET /files/* endpoint and the 'file' envelope type exists in sessionProtocol.ts, but no DownloadButton or download handler component exists in happy-app. Code blocks have a copy button but no download button.
issues.observation_notes: User agent, PO, and architect all independently confirmed no download functionality exists. This is a new feature requirement, not a regression. Server infrastructure partially exists (file serving route).

issues.description: Bug #64: TaskView title duplication -- outer ToolView renders header with tool name, then TaskView renders its own TaskSummary header inside, creating two stacked headers for the same tool call block.
issues.details: ToolView always renders ToolHeader (lines 161-205) showing toolTitle. Then renders SpecificToolView in content area (line 218). For Task/Agent tools, TaskView is the SpecificToolView. TaskView renders TaskSummary which is another visual header. Result: outer header 'Task [icon]' + inner summary '[sub-tool names] [chevron]'. Bug #64 documented in bug-fixes.md as unfixed. Additionally, no visual divider between ToolView header and content area (arch-6).
issues.observation_notes: PO and UI-specialist both identified the duplication via code review. Not browser-verified because no Task/Agent tool call content exists in test sessions. Architect noted the missing divider border between header and content areas.

issues.description: Bug #62: Session title change via change_title MCP shows service message in chat but does not update sidebar or header title. Both sessions show 'root' (working directory basename) instead of the title set via MCP.
issues.details: getSessionName() checks session.metadata?.summary first. The change_title MCP chain: Claude calls change_title -> startHappyServer sends {type:'summary', summary:title} -> apiSession.ts updateMetadata -> server updates metadata -> broadcast to clients. PO confirmed browser: service message 'Title changed to Test: new session creation' visible but header still shows 'root'. The metadata.summary is either not populated, not decrypted correctly, or the sidebar does not re-render on metadata update.
issues.observation_notes: PO and architect independently traced the update chain. Browser-verified: sidebar shows 'root' for both sessions despite one having a title change service message. Bug #62 documented in bug-fixes.md as unfixed.

issues.description: Bug #63: Horizontal scroll indicator hidden on web for both code blocks and tables. Code blocks: showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={false} unconditionally. Tables: showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={Platform.OS !== 'web'} which evaluates to false on web. Users cannot see that content overflows horizontally.
issues.details: Line 187 (code blocks): showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={false} always hidden. Line 308 (tables): showsHorizontalScrollIndicator={Platform.OS !== 'web'} explicitly false on web. The correct behavior for web should be true or use CSS overflow-x styling. Bug #63 documented in bug-fixes.md as unfixed.
issues.observation_notes: PO, architect, and UI-specialist all confirmed via code review. Content is scrollable but no visual indicator shown. Not a blocker but degrades discoverability of scrollable content.

issues.description: Session navigation unreliable: directly navigating to session 2 URL redirects to wrong page (Settings or session 1). Back button from tool detail view sometimes navigates to Inbox or Settings instead of parent session.
issues.details: User agent observed: (1) Navigating to /session/cmnixd68800jxnz15eaw8449j via URL bar redirected to Settings or session 1 on multiple attempts. (2) Back arrow in tool detail view (/session/:id/message/:msgId) navigated to Inbox or Settings instead of returning to the parent session. Both issues suggest routing state corruption when the app has complex navigation history.
issues.observation_notes: User agent browser-verified both navigation issues across multiple attempts. The session 2 content was accessible via sidebar click but not via direct URL navigation. The back button issue may be related to React Navigation stack state management.

issues.description: Bug #61: Mermaid timeline diagrams with Chinese characters or empty events fail to render. Falls back to raw source with 'Mermaid diagram syntax error' message. Previous fix attempt (sanitizeMermaidContent) was reverted.
issues.details: MermaidRenderer uses mermaid.render() and catches errors, showing fallback with raw content. The sanitize approach was attempted but failed. No sanitization code present in current MermaidRenderer.tsx. The mermaid library has known issues with non-ASCII characters in timeline diagrams. Bug #61 documented in bug-fixes.md as 'fix failed'.
issues.observation_notes: PO confirmed via code review. Standard Mermaid flowcharts render correctly (browser-verified by user agent and architect). Only timeline diagrams with Chinese characters are affected.

issues.description: Send button triggers microphone permission dialog when input is empty. No visual indicator that the button changes function (send vs voice) based on input state.
issues.details: User agent browser-verified: clicking send button with empty input triggers 'Microphone Access Required' native browser dialog. Console error logged: 'Web microphone permission denied: {}'. First-time users would expect clicking send with empty input to do nothing, not request microphone access.
issues.observation_notes: User agent verified in browser. Minor UX confusion but the button technically works as designed (it becomes a voice input button when text is empty). The issue is the lack of visual differentiation between send and voice states.

issues.description: Main JS bundle 7.4MB uncompressed served without gzip from nginx. Total initial JS payload ~10.2MB. Missing nginx gzip_static configuration.
issues.details: Architect measured: main bundle 7,747,175 bytes, common chunk 2,425,868 bytes. curl -sI showed no Content-Encoding header. With gzip compression (~3-4x ratio), total would drop to ~2.5-3.4MB. Page load measured at ~50ms (cached) but cold first-visit load severely impacted.
issues.observation_notes: Architect confirmed via network analysis. All static JS served uncompressed.

issues.description: console.log('isToolUseError', tool.result) left in production ToolView.tsx. Leaks tool output content to browser console when tools error.
issues.details: Unguarded console.log fires on tool error state. May expose sensitive tool result data. App has console suppression at startup but the statement remains a code quality issue.
issues.observation_notes: Architect and UI-specialist both found via code review.

skipped_issues.skip_reason: Intentional design decision documented in code. typesRaw.ts:560 explicitly returns null with explanatory comment. Not a bug -- deliberate deferral. TaskView handles subagent content aggregation separately.

skipped_issues.skip_reason: Cannot verify rendering with existing session data. The code-level issue (wrap rendering) is already captured as triage_index 2. start/stop are intentionally not rendered.

skipped_issues.skip_reason: Subsumed by triage_index 5 (Bug #64 TaskView fixes). The divider issue applies to all tool views and should be addressed as part of the ToolView/TaskView cleanup.

pm_notes.description: File upload feature has full backend infrastructure (server upload endpoint, useAttachments hook, AttachmentStrip component) but UI wiring in AgentInput.tsx was lost during merge. This is a reconnection task, not a new feature build.
LaTeX fix is small-effort: import LatexRenderer in MarkdownView.tsx and add an else-if branch for block.type === 'latex'. All other components (parser, renderer) are already correctly implemented.

Enter key behavior conflict: MultiTextInput.tsx submitBehavior='newline' at line 222 conflicts with agentInputEnterToSend default=true in settings.ts:89. The native textarea processes the newline before React event handler fires.
Navigation reliability issues (session URL redirect, back button misdirection) suggest routing state corruption in React Navigation stack. Multiple agents reported related symptoms.
PO reports Bug #64 tool call clickability inside TaskView may already be fixed in current code (ChildMessageBlock passes messageId). Needs live verification with Task tool call content.

strategic_notes: Cycle 1 after major merge with origin. 13 actionable issues across 3 tiers. The top 4 issues (LaTeX, file upload, wrap envelope, Enter key) are all small-to-medium effort with clear code-level root causes identified by multiple agents. File download (triage_index 4) is the largest effort item as a new feature. Bug #64 TaskView issues may be partially resolved already. The session navigation issues (triage_index 8) suggest deeper routing state management problems that may require investigation beyond a point fix. Recommend prioritizing the 4 quick rendering/interaction fixes first (indices 0-3), then the feature gaps (4-5), then the Tier 2 bug fixes.
